drafts.title: UK BEV ~29.8% Aug → US payment+insurance+home charge
drafts.angle: UK August BEV share ~29.8% (SMMT). Not a UK politics lecture. US kitchen-table: when choice expands, shop payment + insurance + home charge before the shiny sticker.
bullets: SMMT: August 2026 UK BEV registrations 28,063; BEV market share 29.8% (up from 26.5% Aug 2025); total new cars 94,236.
Year-to-date through August: BEV share ~25.6% (355,746 BEVs of 1,388,735 cars).
SMMT notes August is a recurring seasonal spike and September plate-change is the key volume test.
Reuters / New AutoMotive framing: August BEV roughly largest single fuel type near 30% share in some counts.
US household takeaway: competition + lease ladders matter more than a foreign mandate story. Soft-pedal Mon Tesla-50% LIVE.
drafts.body:
Britain just printed a loud month for battery EVs.

Industry data from the SMMT puts August battery-electric share at about 29.8 percent. Roughly 28,000 BEVs out of about 94,000 new cars. Year to date the BEV share sits nearer 25.6 percent. August always spikes a bit when overall volume is thinner. September's plate change is when the industry says the real volume test arrives.

That is a UK scoreboard. You live in the US. The usable lesson is not a mandate debate.

When a market gets more EV choice, families win only if the MONTHLY stack is honest: payment, insurance quote on the same VIN, and a real home or apartment charge plan. A pretty range sticker does not pay the electric bill or the premium.

US kitchen-table take for a 42-year-old commuting in Colorado, or a 58-year-old replacing a paid-off sedan:

1) Get the out-the-door payment in writing for the exact trim.
2) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
3) Map weekday charging: Level 2 at home, workplace, or a curbside/garage plan if you rent.
4) Road-trip once on a public charger so you know the app and the rate before the first holiday.

35-54 line: nearly 30 percent of new UK cars in August were battery electric. Your win is the same math in dollars at your dealer and on your bill.

55+ line: more choice only helps if the payment, insurance, and plug plan keep your independence without draining savings.

drafts.title: TX EIA solar>coal 2026 → evening bill plan
drafts.angle: EIA: ERCOT utility-scale solar forecast ~78 billion kWh in 2026 vs coal ~60 billion kWh. First annual solar>coal year on the Texas grid that serves most of the state. Kitchen-table: more midday solar does not automatically cut YOUR evening bill unless you shift loads or have a charge plan.
bullets: EIA Today in Energy (May 13, 2026): ERCOT solar generation forecast 78 BkWh in 2026 vs coal 60 BkWh; first annual surplus of solar over coal.
EIA: Texas expected to host ~40% of US utility-scale solar capacity additions in 2026; Tehuacana Creek 1 Solar+BESS cited at ~837 MW among large projects.
ERCOT July 2026 ops overview: unofficial peak demand record ~91,134 MW on 7/22/2026 (hour ending 18).
Reporting also notes summer solar production records in the mid-30 GW range on hot days (operator/press tallies).
Soft-pedal Fri ERCOT RTC+B battery-market LIVE; this post is solar-vs-coal annual scoreboard + household checklist.
drafts.body:
Texas is rewriting its power mix on paper that matters for the whole country.

The US Energy Information Administration forecasts that in 2026, utility-scale solar on the ERCOT grid (most of Texas) will make about 78 billion kilowatt-hours. Coal is forecast nearer 60 billion. That would be the first year solar beats coal on an annual basis in that system.

Hot summer days already showed how much midday solar the grid can push. ERCOT also printed a huge July demand peak near 91,000 megawatts. Big grids can set records and still leave a household staring at an evening bill.

US kitchen-table take for a 45-year-old in Dallas with a heat pump and an EV, or a 62-year-old in Houston watching the summer bill:

More solar on the grid is good news for supply. It is not a free pass on your meter. Midday power is often the cheap hour. Evening is when AC and cooking stack up.

Independence checklist:

1) Ask your utility or competitive retailer for the real peak window on your rate.
2) Shift dishwasher, laundry, and EV charge into cheaper hours when you can.
3) If you rent, map workplace or curbside charging so you are not stuck on expensive public DC every week.
4) If you own, get a written solar/battery quote that shows bill savings under YOUR rate, not a national average.

35-54 line: Texas solar is on track to out-produce coal for the year. Your job is still the evening bill.

55+ line: grid news is interesting. Your thermostat schedule and charge plan are what keep independence.

drafts.title: CA remote inspection / $600–$1,000 soft costs
drafts.angle: AB 1738 Remote Virtual Inspection Act on Gov. Newsom's desk (sign-by ~Sep 30). Lets homeowners/contractors request remote virtual inspections for residential solar (roughly up to 15 kW), batteries, heat pumps, roofs. SPUR-style estimates: waiting on a 15-minute inspection can add $600-$1,000. Pocketbook soft-cost cut, not a politics fight.
bullets: Canary Media (Sep 14, 2026): AB 1738 and SB 222 on Newsom's desk; deadline ~Sep 30.
AB 1738: right to request remote virtual inspection; larger cities/counties must offer by Jan 1, 2028; in-person still allowed when needed.
SPUR / Solar.com reporting: contractors can wait 2-6 hours for a ~15-minute inspection; wasted time often passed to customer at ~$600-$1,000 per job.
Coverage includes rooftop solar (often cited ≤15 kW), home batteries, heat pump HVAC/water heaters, new roofs.
~19 CA jurisdictions already do remote inspections; LA County reports a large share already remote.
drafts.body:
A lot of the cost of home solar is not the panels.

It is the soft costs: permits, waiting on inspectors, truck rolls, and days of idle crew time that show up on your quote.

California lawmakers sent Assembly Bill 1738 to the governor. It would give homeowners and contractors a right to ask for a remote virtual inspection on common upgrades: rooftop solar in the typical home size band, home batteries, heat pumps, and roofs. Bigger cities and counties would have to offer that option by 2028. Inspectors can still require an in-person visit when safety needs it.

Why your wallet cares: analyses tied to the bill say crews sometimes wait hours for a fifteen-minute check. That idle time often lands as about $600 to $1,000 extra on a project. Multiply that by a state and you get real money families never see on a panel sticker.

US kitchen-table take for a 48-year-old in Riverside County shopping solar, or a 60-year-old who wants the quote without mystery fees:

Ask every installer for a line item called soft costs or permitting. Ask whether your city already offers remote inspection today. Do not sign a change-order for "inspection delays" you never agreed to.

Independence checklist:

1) Get soft costs itemized before deposit.
2) Confirm city/county remote-inspection status in writing.
3) Size the system for your bill, not a brochure.
4) If you are outside California, ask your state or city the same question. Soft costs travel.

35-54 line: cutting $600 to $1,000 of wait-time fluff is how more families actually flip the switch.

55+ line: fewer truck rolls and fewer surprise fees keep the project from eating the emergency fund.

drafts.title: NYC It's Electric +600 curbside L2 for renters
drafts.angle: NYC DOT selecting Brooklyn's It's Electric to expand PlugNYC from ~88 Level 2 curbside points toward ~700 over three years (~600 new). Installations targeted Q1 2027 after design review. Public comment on sites through ~Sep 30, 2026. Apartment/renter independence without a driveway.
bullets: NYC DOT / press: expand from 88 L2 curbside points to nearly 700; ~600 new points across five boroughs over ~3 years.
It's Electric + partner awarded install (~$55.3M) and operate (~$4.9M) contracts per Gothamist reporting.

First neighborhoods named include Soundview/Unionport (Bronx); Rego Park, Forest Hills, Far Rockaway (Queens); Red Hook, Carroll Gardens, Bedford-Stuyvesant (Brooklyn); Upper West Side, Washington Heights (Manhattan); Stapleton (Staten Island).
Also: 92 DC fast + 180 L2 at municipal lots/garages in related DOT buildout.
Comment window on proposed locations cited through Sep 30, 2026; install start often framed Q1 2027.
drafts.body:
If you rent in a big city, the number-one EV blocker is not the car. It is the plug.

New York City is expanding PlugNYC curbside Level 2 charging from about 88 points toward roughly 700 over three years. Brooklyn company It's Electric won the job to replace the pilot gear and add about 600 new charging points across all five boroughs. City reporting puts install and operate contracts in the tens of millions. First neighborhoods lean toward dense housing, tight off-street parking, and lots of taxi and rideshare drivers.

That is not a suburban driveway story. It is a renter and walk-up story.

US kitchen-table take for a 40-year-old in Queens without a garage, or a 55-year-old in Brooklyn who wants out of gas price swings:

Curbside Level 2 will not fill a battery in twenty minutes. It can cover overnight or long curb sessions the way a lamp post covers a block. Pair it with workplace charging when you can. Use DC fast for road trips, not for every Tuesday.

Independence checklist:

1) Comment on proposed sites in your neighborhood before the window closes if you live in one of the listed areas.
2) Price public L2 vs home charging honestly if you ever get a deeded spot.
3) Ask your building about garage Level 2 before you assume curbside is your only path.
4) Other US cities: watch this playbook. Dense housing needs plugs on the curb, not lectures.

35-54 line: six hundred more curbside plugs is how apartment households join the cheap-fill club.

55+ line: you should not need a suburban garage to stop buying gas every week.

Premium and Standard trims come later (Premium late 2026; Standard framed ~$44,990-$48,490 into 2027). Family checklist: demo, payment, insurance, home charge. drafts.body:
You can finally drive the Rivian R2 instead of only watching videos.

Rivian opened demo drives at Spaces. Book on the site or app with your ZIP. Early slots fill fast. That is normal for a new model.

Important money fact: the first trim you can actually buy is the Performance. Press walk-throughs put that near $58,000 before destination and taxes. Premium is expected later this year. Standard is framed for 2027 at a lower entry price near the mid-$40,000s in Rivian's ladder. If the Standard payment is what your household needs, do not let a Performance demo stampede you into the wrong trim.

US kitchen-table take for a 44-year-old with two kids and a road-trip weekend, or a 59-year-old downsizing from a gas SUV:

1) Book the demo. Feel the seats and the cargo.
2) Ask for the out-the-door payment on the trim you can actually order today AND the timing for cheaper trims.
3) Quote insurance on the VIN or configuration before you put money down.
4) Map home or apartment charging. Adventure branding does not charge the battery.

35-54 line: demo the truck. Buy the payment you can sleep on.

55+ line: wait for the Standard trim if that is the independence math. Hype is not a budget.

drafts.title: Plug In America LFP chemistry peace-of-mind
drafts.angle: Plug In America explainer on battery chemistries: LFP (lithium iron phosphate) generally more thermally stable than nickel-rich NMC; higher runaway temperature threshold; oxygen held more tightly. Not "fireproof." Shopping and insurance peace-of-mind for families. Soft-pedal fearmongering.
bullets: Plug In America: LFP vs NMC; LFP strong phosphate-oxygen bonds; higher temperature threshold before thermal runaway in common explainers.
PIA framing: both can fail in rare abuse cases; design, cooling, monitoring still matter.
Consumer translation: many mass-market EVs and home storage favor LFP for cost + stability; long-range packs often still use nickel-rich chemistries.
Ask the dealer/OEM which chemistry is in YOUR trim. It can change by year and market.
Insurance / HOA / garage: honest answers beat viral videos.
drafts.body:
Most families do not need a chemistry lecture. They need one clear shopping question.

What battery chemistry is in this exact car or home pack?

Plug In America walks through why lithium iron phosphate (LFP) is generally more thermally stable than common nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) packs. The phosphate structure holds oxygen tighter. It usually takes more heat and abuse before things go wrong. That does not mean LFP is magic or fireproof. Cooling, software, and crash design still matter. It does mean "safer chemistry" is a real product difference, not a slogan.

US kitchen-table take for a 46-year-old parking in a condo garage, or a 63-year-old putting a pack on the wall near the laundry:

1) Ask the seller: LFP or nickel-rich? Get it in writing for that VIN or that battery SKU.
2) Ask your insurer if the chemistry or UL listing changes the quote.
3) For home storage, ask about placement rules and required clearances.
4) Ignore scare posts that treat every EV the same. Ask for the pack in YOUR driveway.

35-54 line: chemistry is part of the payment stack now, same as range and warranty.

55+ line: peace of mind is independence. Ask the question before you wire a deposit.

drafts.title: NJ community solar ≥15% bill credits (no roof)
drafts.angle: Community solar = subscribe to an off-site array; utility posts bill credits; you pay the provider less than credit value. NJ program: guaranteed discount at least ~15% (LMI often higher under expansion). NY CDG: credits on utility bill; dual or consolidated billing. Soft-pedal PSE&G battery GridSmart; this is bill-credit solar for people without a roof.
bullets: NJ Clean Energy / explainers: Community Solar Energy Program; residential subscribers get bill credits; discounts commonly guaranteed ≥15%; LMI paths often ≥25% under 2026 expansion framing.
PSE&G community solar page: allocated kWh show as Community Solar Credit; some non-bypassable charges may not be credited.
NYSEG / NYSERDA: Community Distributed Generation; find projects via NYSERDA tools; dual-bill vs consolidated/net-crediting models.
Typical honest savings bands in explainers: often mid-single-digits to mid-teens percent depending on state and contract. Read the exit clause.
No panels on your roof. Utility still delivers power.
drafts.body:
You do not need a sunny roof or a landlord's blessing to touch solar savings.

Community solar means a project is built somewhere else on the local grid. You subscribe. The utility applies bill credits for your share. You pay the community-solar company a bit less than those credits are worth. The gap is your savings. Nothing gets bolted to your balcony unless you want that separate product.

New Jersey's permanent program is built around guaranteed bill-credit discounts of at least about 15 percent for standard subscribers, with stronger discounts for qualifying low- and moderate-income households under the expansion rules. New York uses community distributed generation with credits on the utility bill. Some plans send two bills. Some fold the fee into one net credit. Read which one you are signing.

US kitchen-table take for a 38-year-old renter in Newark, or a 70-year-old in a shaded bungalow near Albany:

1) Use the official find-a-project tools, not a cold Facebook ad alone.
2) Ask: guaranteed discount percent, contract length, exit fee, and whether credits cover supply only or delivery too.
3) Confirm your utility territory matches the project.
4) Keep a baseline bill PDF before you enroll so you can see if the savings are real.

35-54 line: fifteen percent off the electric bill without a roof is how renters join the solar club.

55+ line: no ladders, no roof holes, no landlord fight. Just a contract you can read and cancel rules you understand.

drafts.title: Kia Niro EV ~$269/mo lease ladder (not Bolt)
drafts.angle: National lease chatter for 2026 Kia Niro EV Wind near $269/mo for 24 months with ~$3,999 due (qualified; 10k mi/yr common). Also watch 36-month ~$299 variants. Soft-pedal Chevy Bolt $419 LIVE overnight. Soft-pedal Kia EV3 standing avoid. Deadline pressure: many Sep programs end ~Sep 30 / Oct 1. Shop miles, due-at-signing, and insurance.
bullets: Complete Car Lease / EV deal roundups (Sep 2026): Niro EV Wind national programs listed around $269/mo 24 mo / $3,999 due; also $299/mo 36 mo variants; end dates near Oct 1.
Dealer/OEM fine print varies: acquisition fee, taxes, 10,000 mi/yr, excess mileage fees, credit tier.
Electrek lease guide and GM Authority confirm SEPARATE Bolt national lease (~$419/36 mo / ~$5,119 due) through Sep 30. Already LIVE on @UpgradeAmerican overnight. Do not rehash as fresh.
Also on boards: Ioniq 5 SE ~$329/24 mo class offers. Optional second ladder rung if Brian wants a twin post later.
Always confirm on kia.com / dealer worksheet the day you sign.
drafts.body:
If you want a normal-size electric crossover without a luxury payment, look at the September lease board carefully.

Right now one of the loudest national numbers is the Kia Niro EV Wind in the neighborhood of $269 a month for 24 months with about $3,999 due at signing for well-qualified shoppers. Some 36-month versions land nearer $299. Miles are often capped around 10,000 a year. Taxes and fees sit on top. Not every ZIP and credit tier sees the headline.

Why this post is not a Bolt rehash: the Bolt lease chatter is already out there. This is the lower monthly rung on the same shopping week.

US kitchen-table take for a 41-year-old replacing a compact SUV, or a 57-year-old who wants predictable payments:

1) Get the worksheet: monthly, due at signing, miles, excess mile fee, acquisition fee.
2) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
3) Map home or workplace Level 2. A cheap lease with expensive public DC every week is not cheap.
4) Delivery deadline: many September programs want you to take delivery by month-end or Oct 1. Do not assume the number survives next week.

35-54 line: $269-class money is how more households test an EV without a $700 payment.

55+ line: short lease, known miles, written insurance quote. That is independence with a back door.
